L3: type PyFrameObject【1†¶】
L4:     Part of the 【2†Limited API】 (as an opaque struct).
L5: 
L6: The C structure of the objects used to describe frame objects.
L7: 
L8: There are no public members in this structure.
L9: 
L10: Changed in version 3.11: The members of this structure were removed from the public C API. Refer to the 【3†What’s New entry】 for details.
L11: 
L12: The 【4†`PyEval_GetFrame()`】 and 【5†`PyThreadState_GetFrame()`】 functions can be used to get a frame object.
L13: 
L14: See also 【6†Reflection】.

L17: 
L18: The type of frame objects. It is the same object as 【9†`types.FrameType`】 in the Python layer.
L19: 
L20: Changed in version 3.11: Previously, this type was only available after including `<frameobject.h>`.

L118: ## Frame locals proxies【38†¶】
L119: 
L120: Added in version 3.13.
L121: 
L122: The 【30†`f_locals`】 attribute on a 【39†frame object】 is an instance of a “frame-locals proxy”. The proxy object exposes a write-through view of the underlying locals dictionary for the frame. This ensures that the variables exposed by `f_locals` are always up to date with the live local variables in the frame itself.
L123: 
L124: See 【35†PEP 667†peps.python.org】 for more information.
L125: 
L126: 【7†PyTypeObject】 PyFrameLocalsProxy_Type【36†¶】
L127: The type of frame 【34†`locals()`】 proxy objects.
L128:

L130: 
L131:

L133: ## Legacy local variable APIs【41†¶】
L134: 
L135: These APIs are 【42†soft deprecated】. As of Python 3.13, they do nothing. They exist solely for backwards compatibility.
L136: 
L137: void PyFrame_LocalsToFast(【1†PyFrameObject】 *f, int clear)【43†¶】
L138: Prior to Python 3.13, this function would copy the 【30†`f_locals`】 attribute of f to the internal “fast” array of local variables, allowing changes in frame objects to be visible to the interpreter. If clear was true, this function would process variables that were unset in the locals dictionary.
L139: 
L140: 【42†Soft deprecated】 since version 3.13: This function now does nothing.
L141: 
L142: void PyFrame_FastToLocals(【1†PyFrameObject】 *f)【44†¶】
L143: Prior to Python 3.13, this function would copy the internal “fast” array of local variables (which is used by the interpreter) to the 【30†`f_locals`】 attribute of f, allowing changes in local variables to be visible to frame objects.
L144: 
L145: 【42†Soft deprecated】 since version 3.13: This function now does nothing.
L146: 
L147: int PyFrame_FastToLocalsWithError(【1†PyFrameObject】 *f)【45†¶】
L148: Prior to Python 3.13, this function was similar to 【44†`PyFrame_FastToLocals()`】, but would return `0` on success, and `-1` with an exception set on failure.
L149: 
L150: 【42†Soft deprecated】 since version 3.13: This function now does nothing.

L191: const 【7†PyTypeObject】 *PyUnstable_ExecutableKinds【53†¶】
L192: 
L193: 
L194: This is 【50†Unstable API】. It may change without warning in minor releases.
L195: 
L196: An array of executable kinds (executor types) for frames, used for internal debugging and tracing.
L197: 
L198: Tools like debuggers and profilers can use this to identify the type of execution context associated with a frame (such as to filter out internal frames). The entries are indexed by the following constants:
L199: 
L200: Constant  | Description
L201: --- | ---
L202: PyUnstable_EXECUTABLE_KIND_SKIP【54†¶】
L203:     This is 【50†Unstable API】. It may change without warning in minor releases.
L204:  | The frame is internal (For example: inlined) and should be skipped by tools.
L205: 
L206: PyUnstable_EXECUTABLE_KIND_PY_FUNCTION【55†¶】
L207:     This is 【50†Unstable API】. It may change without warning in minor releases.
L208:  | The frame corresponds to a standard Python function.
L209: PyUnstable_EXECUTABLE_KIND_BUILTIN_FUNCTION【56†¶】
L210:     This is 【50†Unstable API】. It may change without warning in minor releases.
L211:  | The frame corresponds to a function defined in native code.
L212: 
L213: PyUnstable_EXECUTABLE_KIND_METHOD_DESCRIPTOR【57†¶】
L214:     This is 【50†Unstable API】. It may change without warning in minor releases.
L215:  | The frame corresponds to a method on a class instance.
L216: 
L217: Note that reading the executable kind from a frame is currently only possible with undocumented internal APIs.
L218: Added in version 3.13.
